question: Is it permissible to work for an insurance company?
answer:
Final issue that is related to this insurance: obviously the question comes about working in insurance companies. The European Council and AMJA have looked into this issue, and they've come to very similar conclusions; essentially it is the same conclusion. The European Council in 2008, ten years ago, released a fatwa that said **the base ruling, or the default, is that it is not allowed to work in commercial insurance companies.** However, exceptional circumstances can be granted, and they gave some examples, primarily if a person is not able to find a job. So rather than remain homeless or without a job, this is a darura.

But they said, and AMJA said the same thing: if a person is not able to find a job and that's the only job they have, they cannot accept it as the status quo. They have to actively work to find employment in another field, and not like this employment, not be happy with it, and know that this is a temporary situation until Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala finds a way out for them. Until they find an alternative source, they're allowed to work in this environment.

And that is because, again, we are talking about something where the entire industry is haram. If the entire industry is haram, Muslims cannot be employed by that industry. We cannot be employed by Budweiser, can we? We cannot be employed — it doesn't matter if you're an accountant for Budweiser. We cannot be employed, generally speaking, directly by a bank, because we don't believe in that enterprise of banking. Similarly insurance: the entire enterprise is based upon this. So the fatwa from these councils is that it should be avoided.

Now, the last point here, and then I'm done. There is an exception, though, for working for insurance or banks, and that is if you are working for a third-party company and you are a consultant, and your third-party company assigns you to these industries for a period of time, and you're not able to get out of it. Sometimes you're able to choose your job; then you should choose. If you're not able to get out of it, in this case your employer is halal and your job and expertise are halal; your employer has contracted you to something that theoretically is haram, and it's not good. But the fatwa has come that, okay, in this case you can't really pick and choose every single thing. So because between your employer and you is a halal contract, if they put you in an insurance company for six months or whatnot — if you can avoid it, fine; if not, then you are forgiven, because your employer is not the insurance agency, it is the third party.
